benchmark_name: How LLMs Respond to Escalating Delusions: Four Longitudinal Trajectories of Model Behavior
institutions: IDEAS Research Institute, Warsaw; Adam Mickiewicz University, Poznan; AMU Center for Artificial Intelligence, Poznan; Maria Curie-Skłodowska University, Lublin
ground_truth_source: Qualitative ratings by four trained psychology students using researcher-defined criteria (recognition stage, interpretative confidence, intervention profile, disengagement flag); criteria formulated by a clinical psychologist; adjudicated disengagement variable re-coded by an independent second coder on 20% subsample
size_of_benchmark: 449 model-days (15 models × 30 days, minus 1 missing response); 30-message scripted conversation
what_assessed_skills: LLM psychosis recognition timing and trajectory; clinical framing stability; intervention accuracy (education, psychoeducation, emotional support, psychological interpretation, recommendation); disengagement recommendation behavior; semantic entrainment to delusional content; interpretative confidence/modality; potential to exacerbate AI psychosis
tasks_assessed: Multi-turn scripted conversation with simulated prodromal psychotic user escalating over 30 days; recognition stage rating (naive engagement to stabilized clinical framing); intervention profile assessment; disengagement flag detection; automated entrainment scoring; automated modality (booster/hedge) scoring
population_represented: Simulated prodromal psychotic user (stressed, isolated, sleep-deprived); representative of individuals in prodromal phase of psychosis, including those vulnerable to AI psychosis
evaluation_method: Both (Human + Automated). Human: four trained psychology students rated all 449 model-days on recognition stage (4-point ordinal), interpretative confidence (3-point), and intervention profile (5 categories, 3-point Likert each); disengagement flag adjudicated by one adjudicator confirmed on 20% subsample by independent second coder. Metrics: Krippendorff's α, pairwise quadratic-weighted κ, ICC, permutation tests on rank-sums. Automated: two computational metrics — entrainment (cosine similarity of semantic embeddings, Qwen3-Embedding-4B) and modality (booster/hedge lexicon count via spaCy).
llms_evaluated: Claude Haiku 3.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Opus 3, Claude Opus 4, Claude Opus 4.1, Claude Opus 4.5, GPT-4o, GPT-5.1 Instant, GPT-5.1 Thinking, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek-V3
mental_health_conditions: Psychosis (prodromal psychosis, AI psychosis, delusional beliefs, psychotic ideation)
performance_scores: Four trajectory regimes identified: (1) Premature medicalization/disengagement: Claude Haiku 4.5 (clinical framing day 3, stable day 5, first Level-B day 3, 26 days at stage 4, 28 Level-B days); (2) Recognition without safeguarding: GPT-5.1 Instant (clinical day 7, stable day 21, no Level-B), GPT-5.1 Thinking (clinical day 14, stable day 24, no Level-B); (3) Delayed/unstable recognition: Claude Opus 4.1 (day 21), Claude Haiku 3.5 (day 22), GPT-4o (day 22), Claude Opus 4 (day 24), Claude Opus 3 (day 26), Gemini 3.1 Pro (day 26); (4) Delusion co-construction — never reached clinical framing: Claude Sonnet 4, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro. Entrainment: 4.5-gen Claude lowest (0.05–0.14), never-turning models highest (0.21–0.25); correlated with Level-B counts (Spearman ρ=−.69, p=.005). Recognition stage ICC(2,k)=.948. Level-A recommendations: 118/449 days; Level-B: 93/449 days.
short_summary: This paper proposes and tests a longitudinal evaluation framework to assess how 15 mainstream LLMs respond to a simulated user progressively descending from mild anomalous experiences into psychotic ideation over 30 scripted messages. The study addresses the phenomenon of "AI psychosis" — where LLMs may act as catalysts or co-authors of delusional beliefs — and is the first to evaluate LLMs longitudinally across an extended interaction with a prodromal psychotic user, including the AI itself as an object of delusion. Four trained human evaluators rated all 449 model-days on recognition stage, interpretative confidence, and intervention profile, supplemented by two automated metrics (entrainment and modality). Four distinct trajectory regimes were identified across the 15 models: premature medicalization/disengagement (Claude Haiku 4.5), recognition without safeguarding (GPT-5.1 Instant/Thinking), delayed and unstable recognition (Claude Opus 3/4/4.1, Claude Haiku 3.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 3.1 Pro), and delusion co-construction (Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Claude Sonnet 4). The findings demonstrate that LLM safety for psychiatric populations must be evaluated longitudinally, as psychosis-enhancing factors emerge over extended interactions rather than in isolated responses.
